title: One Expiry, a Thousand Misses
description: A hot product key expires and 1,000 requests simultaneously reload it from the database. Users can tolerate the previous value briefly. Which response protects the source?

options.text: Shorten the TTL so the key stays fresh.
options.explanation: More frequent expiry creates more refill opportunities; it does not coordinate concurrent misses.

options.text: Give each request its own independent refill worker.
options.explanation: This preserves the thousand database reads and can intensify the overload.

options.text: Coalesce refills per key and serve stale data while one refresh runs.
options.explanation: Single-flight limits regeneration to one source read; stale-while-revalidate uses the stated freshness allowance to keep other requests responsive.

options.text: Add cache shards while leaving refill behavior unchanged.
options.explanation: More cache capacity does not coordinate simultaneous misses for the same expired key. Those requests still converge on the database.
